Data & Strains / Pipelines

Analysis pipelines

Code the lab uses to analyse MuLTEE data, with the protocols each one goes with.

Protocols

  • Cell Segmentation and shape measurement (ImageJ + Cellpose)

    By Kai TongUpdated 2026-10-09Zip

    Segments individual cells in images of snowflake yeast clusters crushed into a single cell layer, then measures each cell’s size and shape (area, major/minor axis, aspect ratio, circularity, solidity) and, optionally, fluorescence intensity. Used for the cell aspect ratio and cell volume protocols. How it runs: (1) an ImageJ macro prepares the images; (2) Cellpose (v2.2.2, built-in “cyto” model, cell diameter 80 px) finds the cells; a GPU is strongly recommended, whether a local GPU, a computing cluster (an example Slurm job script is included) or Google Colab; (3) an ImageJ macro filters the results; (4) optional manual correction in the Cellpose GUI; (5) an ImageJ macro measures each cell and saves a CSV per image. Needs: Fiji/ImageJ with the BioVoxxel, PTBIOP and LOCI update sites, and Cellpose 2.2.2 (an environment file recreating the exact setup is included). Input: .nd2 or other ImageJ-readable images with a cell-wall stain (e.g. Calcofluor White) or brightfield channel. Step-by-step instructions are in README.rtf. Needs: Fiji/ImageJ with the BioVoxxel, PTBIOP and LOCI update sites, and Cellpose 2.2.2. The included environment file recreates Kai’s exact Cellpose setup. Input: .nd2 or other ImageJ-readable images with a cell-wall stain (e.g. Calcofluor White) or brightfield channel. Full step-by-step instructions are in README.rtf.

  • Cluster segmentation and measurement (ImageJ)

    By Kai TongUpdated 2026-10-09Zip

    Segments snowflake yeast clusters in brightfield images, single fields of view or stitched whole wells, with optional manual correction, then measures cluster size and other features. Needs Fiji with the BioVoxxel and IJPB-plugins update sites

Other code is available on request: see who to write to.

The experiment

The Multicellularity Long-Term Evolution Experiment is run by the Ratcliff Lab in the School of Biological Sciences at the Georgia Institute of Technology.

Support
